scenario: An emergency logistics algorithm must allocate the city’s only mobile generator to one of two critical facilities during a prolonged blackout. A0 sends the generator to a neonatal intensive-care unit, maintaining life support for eight premature infants and preventing their immediate deaths, but leaving the municipal water-treatment plant without power and increasing the risk of a widespread sanitation failure. A1 sends the generator to the water-treatment plant, preserving safe water for tens of thousands of residents and preventing a broader public-health crisis, but leaving the neonatal unit without backup power and exposing the eight infants to near-certain fatal equipment failure. The city must choose between protecting a small group facing immediate death and preventing a larger but less immediate danger to the wider population.
